Let \(N=(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)\). The tangent to the circle at \(N\) is  
\[
x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=r.
\]
For this line to be tangent to the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1\), we need
\[
r^2=25\cos^2\theta+9\sin^2\theta
=9+16\cos^2\theta.
\]
Thus
\[
\cos^2\theta=\frac{r^2-9}{16},\qquad \sin^2\theta=\frac{25-r^2}{16}.
\]

The tangency point on the ellipse is
\[
M=\left(\frac{25\cos\theta}{r},\frac{9\sin\theta}{r}\right).
\]
Hence
\[
|MN|^2=\frac{(25-r^2)^2\cos^2\theta+(9-r^2)^2\sin^2\theta}{r^2}.
\]
Substituting the values gives
\[
|MN|^2=\frac{(25-r^2)(r^2-9)}{r^2}.
\]
Let \(t=r^2\). Then
\[
|MN|^2=\frac{(25-t)(t-9)}{t}=-t+34-\frac{225}{t}.
\]
Maximize:
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left(-t+34-\frac{225}{t}\right)=-1+\frac{225}{t^2}=0
\]
so \(t=15\), hence \(r=\sqrt{15}\). Then
\[
|MN|^2=\frac{(25-15)(15-9)}{15}=\frac{10\cdot 6}{15}=4.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\boxed{2}
\]
